# `silk/time/plain_time`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Times of day without a date or a time zone: the [`PlainTime`](#PlainTime) type.

## When to use

Use [`PlainTime`](#PlainTime) for a wall-clock time that is not tied to a day, such as an opening hour or
an alarm at 07:30. For a time on a given day, use `silk.time.plain_date_time`. For a point in
time, use `silk.time.instant`.

## Details

A `PlainTime` has an hour from 0 to 23, a minute and a second from 0 to 59, and a nanosecond
part from 0 to 999,999,999. It has no leap second: second 60 in a text reads as 59.

## `PlainTime`

```silk
pub struct PlainTime
```

A time of day with nanosecond precision, with no date and no time zone.

### Details

The hour is from 0 to 23, the minute and the second from 0 to 59, and the nanosecond part from
0 to 999,999,999. `==`, `!=`, `<`, `<=`, `>`, and `>=` compare times from midnight forward.
`Display` writes `HH:MM:SS`, with a fraction when the nanosecond part is not zero.

<a id="PlainTime.impl.addWrapping"></a>

### Method `addWrapping`

```silk
pub fn addWrapping(self: Self, span: Duration) -> PlainTime
```

Returns the time `span` later on a clock, or earlier for a negative span. The result wraps
around midnight.

#### Details

Whole days in `span` have no effect: `23:30` plus 45 minutes is `00:15`, and so is `23:30`
plus 24 hours and 45 minutes.

<a id="PlainTime.impl.round"></a>

### Method `round`

```silk
pub fn round(self: Self, step: TimeIncrement, mode: RoundingMode) -> PlainTime
```

Returns the time rounded to a multiple of `step` from midnight, going around midnight.

#### Details

`23:59:40` rounded to the nearest minute is `00:00`. To keep the day that the rounding
reaches, round a `PlainDateTime`.

#### Examples

```silk
import silk.time.plain_time { PlainTime }
import silk.time.rounding { RoundingMode, TimeIncrement, TimeUnit }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let time = PlainTime.make(9, 7, 31, 0)
  let rounded = time.round(TimeIncrement.of(5, TimeUnit.Minute), RoundingMode.HalfExpand)
  if &rounded != &PlainTime.make(9, 10, 0, 0) {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="PlainTime.impl.parse"></a>

### Associated function `parse`

```silk
pub fn parse(text: string) -> Result<PlainTime, TimeParseError>
```

Reads a time from ISO 8601 text such as `17:36:22.5`.

#### Details

The text is `HH`, `HH:MM`, `HH:MM:SS`, `HHMM`, or `HHMMSS`, with an optional fraction of one
to nine digits after the seconds and an optional prefix `T`. Second `60` reads as `59`. A
numeric UTC offset and bracketed annotations can follow; they are checked and then ignored.
The text can also be a full date and time such as `2026-11-19T17:36:22`, from which the time
is taken.

#### Errors

- `TimeParseReason.UnexpectedEnd` or `UnexpectedCharacter` if the text does not have that
  form.
- `TimeParseReason.OutOfRange` if a field names no real value, such as hour 24.
- `TimeParseReason.MissingTime` if the text is a date without a time.
- `TimeParseReason.Ambiguous` if the text has no prefix `T` and is also a valid year and
  month or month and day, such as `1214` or `2026-11`.
- `TimeParseReason.UtcNotAllowed` if the text has the UTC designator `Z`.
- `TimeParseReason.UnsupportedCalendar` if a calendar annotation is not `[u-ca=iso8601]`.
- `TimeParseReason.UnknownCriticalAnnotation` if an annotation with an unknown key starts
  with `!`.
